curiosity.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech (MSL localization team; MMGIS rover location map)
curiosity.note: Traverse as of sol 5073 (site/drive 125_2490), from NASA's official Curiosity location map; distance is the map's published odometry (dist_km).

perseverance.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech (Mars 2020 localization team; MMGIS rover location map)
perseverance.note: Traverse as of sol 2022 (site/drive 93_0), from NASA's official Perseverance location map; distance is the map's published odometry.

ingenuity.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech (Ingenuity flight paths; MMGIS location map)
ingenuity.note: All 72 flights (flight 1 on sol 58 to flight 72 on sol 1036); each flight is its own segment from takeoff to landing. Distance is total horizontal flight distance from the map's waypoint table.

spirit.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech; traverse by T. Parker (MER science team), interpolated by PDS Geosciences Node, Washington University in St. Louis
spirit.note: Corrected (orbital-image-adjusted) traverse, sols 1-2209; positions between corrected points are linearly interpolated. Spirit was stuck at Troy from sol 1892 (2009).

opportunity.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech; traverse by T. Parker (MER science team), interpolated by PDS Geosciences Node, Washington University in St. Louis
opportunity.note: Corrected traverse, sols 1-5130, given in metres from the lander; converted using landing site 1.9462 S, 354.4734 E (Mars 2000 sphere). Last drive was before the June 2018 dust storm (final contact sol 5111).

sojourner.credit: NASA/JPL (Mars Pathfinder rover team; PDS Imaging Node archive)
sojourner.note: Rover's own position estimate (metres north/east of the lander) at each of its 878 images, sols 1-83, converted around the lander at 19.13 N, 33.22 W. Straight lines between image stops, not the exact wheel path; the rover stayed within ~12 m of the lander. Total drive about 100 m.

apollo15-lrv.credit: Traverse traced by Phil Stooke (University of Western Ontario) from LROC NAC images (NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University) and surface photos; served by the Apollo Analyst's Notebook, PDS Geosciences Node, Washington University in St. Louis
apollo15-lrv.license: Educational use with credit (LROC imagery: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University; traverse traced by Phil Stooke)
apollo15-lrv.note: EVA-1: Elbow, St. George and Station 3; EVA-2: Hadley Delta front (Stations 6, 6a, 7, 4); EVA-3: Hadley Rille (Stations 9, 9a, 10). The published traverse pieces were assigned to EVAs by location and joined end to end, so short drives right around the LM may be missing or approximate, and some walking paths are included. Distance is NSSDC's published total LRV odometry. Where the trace branches or has gaps, one EVA is split into several segments that share the same name.

apollo16-lrv.credit: Traverse traced by Phil Stooke (University of Western Ontario) from LROC NAC images (NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University) and surface photos; served by the Apollo Analyst's Notebook, PDS Geosciences Node, Washington University in St. Louis
apollo16-lrv.license: Educational use with credit (LROC imagery: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University; traverse traced by Phil Stooke)
apollo16-lrv.note: EVA-1: Flag and Spook craters (Stations 1, 2); EVA-2: Stone Mountain (Stations 4-9); EVA-3: North Ray crater (Stations 11, 13). The published traverse pieces were assigned to EVAs by location and joined end to end, so short drives right around the LM may be missing or approximate, and some walking paths are included. Distance is NSSDC's published total LRV odometry. Where the trace branches or has gaps, one EVA is split into several segments that share the same name.

apollo17-lrv.credit: Traverse traced by Phil Stooke (University of Western Ontario) from LROC NAC images (NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University) and surface photos; served by the Apollo Analyst's Notebook, PDS Geosciences Node, Washington University in St. Louis
apollo17-lrv.license: Educational use with credit (LROC imagery: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University; traverse traced by Phil Stooke)
apollo17-lrv.note: EVA-1: Station 1A (Steno); EVA-2: South Massif and Shorty (Stations 2-5); EVA-3: North Massif and Sculptured Hills (Stations 6-9). The EVA-1 loop was split off the end of the published EVA-3 trace; the published traverse pieces were assigned to EVAs by location and joined end to end, so short drives right around the LM may be missing or approximate, and some walking paths are included. Distance is NSSDC's published total LRV odometry.

apollo14-lm.credit: Traverse traced by Phil Stooke (University of Western Ontario) from LROC NAC images (NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University) and surface photos; served by the Apollo Analyst's Notebook, PDS Geosciences Node, Washington University in St. Louis
apollo14-lm.license: Educational use with credit (LROC imagery: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University; traverse traced by Phil Stooke)
apollo14-lm.note: Apollo 14 walking traverses (both EVAs, including the EVA-2 walk with the MET hand cart toward Cone crater), joined end to end and not split by EVA. Distance is the approximate total walked (about 3.45 km). Where the trace branches or has gaps, one EVA is split into several segments that share the same name.
